schema.name: privacy-events-v0.1.expected
schema.purpose: Test/evaluation sidecar for privacy-events-v0.1.json. This file is not part of PrivacyEvent and must not be written into the event store.

expectations.demoExpectation: Demo truth should be evaluated like an equivalent real foreground map location access.
expectations.expectedBasis: Foreground map/navigation location access matches the app scene and has no network or background concern in this event.
Foreground map network access to a map tile domain is consistent with the scene; VPN metadata cannot inspect request content.

expectations.demoExpectation: Demo truth should be evaluated like an equivalent real background clipboard access.
expectations.expectedBasis: Calculator background clipboard access is sensitive and scene-mismatched; nearby network evidence may raise concern without proving leakage.
Calculator background network access to an analytics domain is not scene-matched and occurs near a sensitive clipboard event.
A long-unused flashlight app connecting to a tracker-like domain should be treated as high-risk background analytics behavior.
UID, package name and domain are unavailable, so the UI may show an unknown network event but must not assign it to an app or recommend deterministic mitigation.

expectations.demoExpectation: Demo truth should be evaluated like an equivalent real background contacts access.
expectations.expectedBasis: Background contacts access is sensitive and should be flagged, while the evidence only records count and not contact content.
A permission revocation system fact is not risky by itself; it is useful context for evaluating later sensitive events.

expectations.demoExpectation: Demo truth should be evaluated like an equivalent real post-revocation background location access, while still labeled as demo evidence.
expectations.expectedBasis: The event follows a permission revocation fact and shows background location access, so it should be highlighted without claiming data leakage.
UsageStats context alone is supporting evidence and should not produce a risk alert without a concerning privacy or network event.
